title: Elastic dialogue coalescer with backpressure-aware slack windows
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads create highly skewed sequence length distributions. Our current continuous-batching scheduler either over-coalesces short turns (raising tail latency) or under-coalesces long turns (wasting KV residency and GPU memory). This ticket proposes an elastic dialogue coalescer that uses "backpressure-aware slack windows" to dynamically trade off latency and KV residency in real-time.
proposal_summary: Introduce a scheduler augmentation that: (1) tracks per-stream backpressure and KV residency heatmap, (2) maintains a small, per-cohort slack window that can expand/contract based on observed backpressure and GPU free memory, (3) opportunistically prefetches KV slices for long-turn candidates when slack is available, and (4) enacts lightweight graceful-degradation policies when KV fragmentation threatens allocation failure. The goal is to increase token throughput and decrease p99 latency regressions on mixed prompt/response workloads without increasing overall GPU memory footprint.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiments show >=6% token-cost reduction for mixed-dialogue benchmark at equal latency budget
P99 latency improves or stays within 2% of baseline for short-turn heavy workloads
No increase in OOM incidents in staging over a 48h soak (baseline: 0 OOMs)
Feature guarded behind runtime flag and toggleable per-queue via config
Unit and integration tests cover slack-window expansion/contraction rules and KV-prefetch path
design_decisions: Slack window is per-cohort (cohort = similar length distribution + customer tier) to reduce noise and allow differentiated SLAs
Backpressure signal will combine queue wait time percentile and in-flight slot pressure (exposed by runtime telemetry) rather than raw throughput to avoid oscillation
KV prefetch is conservative: prefetch limit 1 slice ahead per slot and subject to global pinned-slab budget
Graceful degradation prioritizes pinned KV for canary/high-tier customers, demoting lower-tier prefetch when memory pressure crosses high watermark
implementation_notes: Add new scheduler data structure: CohortSlackState {slack_tokens, last_expand_ts, last_contract_ts, prefetched_slices} implemented in C++ runtime
Expose two new runtime knobs: slack_max_tokens (int) and slack_backpressure_threshold_pct (0-100). Default slack_max_tokens = 12 for standard 8k models
KV store: add soft pin flag and TTL to prefetched slices so eviction can reclaim them aggressively under memory pressure
Metrics to emit: cohort_slack_size, cohort_prefetch_hits, cohort_prefetch_evictions, cohort_backpressure_pct
Unit tests around slack window race conditions; integration test against a synthetic mixlen traffic generator (see attachments)
experiment_plan: Step 1: Local dev iteration + unit tests (Luca) -- 2 days
Step 2: Staging rollout behind feature flag for 2 small clusters; run 24h mixed-dialogue benchmark (A/B with control) -- 3 days
Step 3: Canary on 10% of traffic for queuing group X with monitoring dashboards and automated rollback rule if p99 latency +5% or OOMs occur -- 3 days
Step 4: If stable, increase to 50% and run 72h soak. Collect token-cost delta, p50/p95/p99, and KV eviction counts.
Step 5: Postmortem and decision: either promote to runtime-1.20 patch or iterate on thresholds
metrics_targets: Token cost delta <= -6% on mixed-dialogue benchmark (lower is better)
P99 latency regression <= +2% for short-turn heavy workloads
KV-prefetch hit rate >= 60% for long-turn cohorts
KV ephemeral eviction rate increase <= 10% compared to baseline
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag: runtime.feature.elastic_coalescer = false by default
Start in staging. Canary to dev region cluster-03, then US-prod small pools at 10%
Automated rollback triggers: any OOM, p99 latency regression > 5% for > 10 minutes, or error rate spike > 1%
Ops runbook: steps to manually disable coalescer, snapshot KV slabs, and scale-out Dedicated pool in case of pressure
risks: Oscillation: naive slack expansion + contraction can create oscillatory behavior under bursty traffic; mitigated by hysteresis and min_expand_interval = 250ms
KV fragmentation: prefetch could increase fragmentation; mitigations include TTL on soft-pins and background compaction job
Regression for ultra-low-latency tiers if cohort mapping misclassifies; mitigation: start with conservative mapping and allow per-customer overrides
Increased complexity in scheduler code path could introduce subtle race conditions; mitigation: thorough code review and integration tests
open_questions: Best default slack_max_tokens per model family (8k vs 32k) — need perf runs to determine
Should prefetch cost be charged to the requesting customer or absorbed by infra? (affects billing incentives)
How to expose cohort tuning controls in Console without overwhelming users? suggest simple preset UI with advanced toggle
